name: Satellite Imagery
title: Satellite Imagery
answer: Satellite imagery as alternative data means using pictures of the Earth taken from orbit to answer questions that financial and economic analysts care about. The signals are physical and observable: parking lot occupancy at a retail chain, the pace of construction on a new plant, the area under a crop, the glow of a refinery at night, the number of ships waiting at a port. Because the data is collected independently of the companies being studied, it can be gathered before quarterly reports are published. Coverage is global, though the quality of the signal varies with cloud cover, resolution and how often a given location is imaged.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Satellite imagery as alternative data means using pictures of the Earth taken from orbit to answer questions that financial and economic analysts care about. The signals are physical and observable: parking lot occupancy at a retail chain, the pace of construction on a new plant, the area under a crop, the glow of a refinery at night, the number of ships waiting at a port. Because the data is collected independently of the companies being studied, it can be gathered before quarterly reports are published. Coverage is global, though the quality of the signal varies with cloud cover, resolution and how often a given location is imaged.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The raw material comes from two main sources: commercial satellite operators that sell tasking and archive access, and public programs such as the European Space Agency's Sentinel missions and NASA's Landsat, which provide free imagery at moderate resolution. On the ground, the work runs on cloud storage for large image archives, GPU compute for model training and inference, and geospatial libraries for handling coordinates and map projections. A typical pipeline pulls scenes on a schedule, crops them to the areas of interest, and stores derived counts rather than the full imagery. Costs scale with how much area is watched and how frequently it is refreshed.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts start by defining a physical proxy, something visible from orbit that moves with the economic quantity they want to track. They then build a labeled set, often by hand counting objects in a sample of images, and train a detection or segmentation model to find the same objects automatically. Change detection compares images of the same location over time to measure growth, decline or disruption. The resulting counts are cleaned for clouds, shadows and seasonal effects, then aggregated into a time series that can be compared against company disclosures or official statistics. Validation against known figures is what separates a usable signal from a suggestive picture.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Imagery is subject to national licensing rules, export controls and restrictions on how frequently certain locations may be imaged, and some countries limit the resolution that can be sold commercially. Privacy rules in several jurisdictions treat images of identifiable people or private property as sensitive, which pushes providers toward aggregation and away from publishing raw scenes. Provenance matters because a derived number is only as good as the image it came from, so buyers increasingly ask for the capture date, sensor, processing steps and model version behind a series. Contracts typically govern redistribution, and firms that resell signals must respect the original operator's terms. This site tracks 229 compliance and regulation pages covering the wider rules that touch AI-driven data products.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Falling launch costs and smaller satellites are increasing how often any given place is imaged, which shortens the lag between a real world event and a usable signal. Cheaper compute and open pretrained vision models are lowering the barrier for smaller firms to build their own detectors. At the same time, regulators are paying more attention to how such data is collected and resold, and buyers are asking harder questions about accuracy and audit trails. The likely direction is toward more frequent, more automated monitoring with clearer documentation of where each number came from.
